concrete-pictorial-abstract.name: Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract (CPA)
concrete-pictorial-abstract.rationale: Transitions physical objects (counters, bread slices) to sketches before abstract numbers.

think-aloud.name: Think-Aloud & Metacognitive Prompts
think-aloud.rationale: Helps child verbalise their inner reasoning without fear of wrong answers.

worked-examples.name: Worked Examples & Error Analysis
worked-examples.rationale: Looking at solved examples together relieves performance anxiety and clarifies rules.

open-ended-creative.name: Open-Ended Creative Explorations
open-ended-creative.rationale: Harnesses natural curiosity and multiple representations.

activities: Fold a paper napkin into 4 pieces, then fold another into 8 pieces. Lay them side by side to see which single piece is larger.
Share 8 strawberries between 4 soft toys. Count how many each friend receives.
weeks.askYourChild: If more friends come to share the pizza, do the slices get bigger or smaller?

activities: Draw a long chocolate bar on paper. Colour in 1/2 with blue and 1/4 with yellow. Talk about how many 1/4 pieces fit in 1/2.
Find things around the house that are half-full or quarter-full.
weeks.askYourChild: How can we prove that two quarters are the same as one half?

activities: Count 12 spoons. Find half (6 spoons) and one quarter (3 spoons) by making equal piles.
Bake or make toast together, cutting toast into four triangular quarters.
weeks.askYourChild: What is your favourite way to divide a sandwich?

activities: Create a 'Fraction Monster' using cut paper shapes of halves and quarters.
Invent a fraction riddle for someone in your family to solve.
weeks.askYourChild: What was the most surprising thing you discovered about fractions this month?

weeks.focus: Spotting the Value of Hundreds and Tens
activities: Look for 3-digit house numbers or speed signs on a walk. Call out the tens digit.
Make 3-digit numbers using playing cards (Aces = 1, omit 10/face cards).
weeks.askYourChild: In the number 472, what does the 7 really stand for?

weeks.focus: Zero as the Silent Place Holder
activities: Write 58 on paper. Slide a 0 into the middle to make 508. Talk about why the 5 moved to the hundreds place.
Count up by tens starting from 290 to cross into 300.
weeks.askYourChild: What would happen to 508 if the zero fell out of the middle?

activities: Practise splitting numbers: 45 is 40 and 5. Try adding 23 by adding 20 first, then 3.
Estimate prices to the nearest 10 during grocery trips.
weeks.askYourChild: How does your brain like to break up big numbers?

activities: Play 'I am thinking of a 3-digit number with 6 hundreds and an even number of ones'.
Write a secret number code for a grown-up to guess.
weeks.askYourChild: Can you make a tricky number riddle for me?

activities: Look for tessellations and repeating tiles around your home or pavement.
Draw repeating patterns using simple triangles and squares.
weeks.askYourChild: Where can we see math hiding outside today?

activities: Design a board game with cardboard where moving forward requires solving a riddle.
Create a dice game with custom rules for doubling points.
weeks.askYourChild: What rule would make our game the most fun to play?

activities: Estimate how many footsteps it takes to walk from the front door to the kitchen.
Test three different ways to group and count a large jar of pasta shells.
weeks.askYourChild: Which counting shortcut felt the most satisfying?

activities: Build the tallest freestanding tower using only rolled newspaper and tape.
Write or draw an invention that solves a small problem around the house.
weeks.askYourChild: What was the most exciting thing you designed this week?
